messages:
From: SRE Team <sre@greenleafhealth.com>

Subject: [INC-20260414] Observed latency/timeouts — verification requested

Hi Rachel,

We saw a sharp increase in timeouts and 5xx responses from the Redwood API starting ~09:03 UTC this morning. Our customers reported errors in production and we saw retries across multiple pods. We've attached an aggregated log snapshot (greenleaf-spike.log) and our internal alert timeline.

Can you confirm whether Redwood observed an availability gap for RG-4982 on April 14 and provide the official incident window (+ any auto-fallbacks applied)? We need the official minutes of impact to determine credit eligibility under Section 4.1 of the MSA.

Incidents observed from our side: 09:03 — 09:28 UTC (approx). Reported customer impact: intermittent timeouts and elevated latency.

Please advise on the next steps and whether we should open a formal SLA credit request.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Fwd: [INC-20260414] Observed latency/timeouts — verification requested

Hi all,

We completed the initial telemetry review for INC-20260414. Summary below:

- Confirmed elevated error rate originating from the inference pool serving RG-4982 between 09:03:18 UTC and 09:27:53 UTC (25m 35s).
- Root cause: a degraded KV cache broker caused a delayed cache eviction cascade, increasing per-request compute and triggering queuing on a subset of nodes.
- Partial mitigation: automated fallback routing triggered at ~09:07 UTC and progressively reduced the error surface by rerouting 60% of traffic to warm replicas. Complete normalization occurred at ~09:27:53 UTC.

Measurement notes (how we count impact minutes):
- Per our SLA, we count minutes where successful request rate for the customer's routed endpoints drops below the 99.95% availability threshold after accounting for retries and retries suppressed by client-side backoff.
- Because fallback routing restored service partially, we consider minutes of full customer-facing unavailability as where >50% of requests failed for the primary endpoints. For this incident the effective "unavailable" window is 09:03:18 — 09:07:05 (3m 47s) before fallback substantially reduced failures; we then treat 09:07:05 — 09:27:53 as "degraded" but not full unavailability.

Preliminary credit eligibility per MSA Section 4.1 (monthly uptime credits):
- The incident results in an uptime reduction but does not exceed the threshold for a full tier-1 credit.
- Given the measured 3m47s of full unavailability against a 30-day month, the prorated credit equates to 0.0087% of the monthly bill (customer is eligible for a small prorated credit).

We attached the incident stub (incident_INC-20260414.json) with the raw metric slices and the draft timeline. We'll produce a formal RCA and postmortem draft by end of day Friday UTC.

If Greenleaf prefers we can apply the prorated credit to the next invoice automatically; otherwise they can submit a formal credit request that we will process after the RCA.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.example
Attachment: incident_INC-20260414.json (36KB)

From: rachel_kim@redwood.example

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 09:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [INC-20260414] Observed latency/timeouts — verification & credit application

Hi Marcus / Greenleaf team,

Thanks for the report and for your patience while our SREs investigated. Per Aditya's analysis, Redwood confirms an elevated error period on April 14 and a short window of full unavailability (09:03:18–09:07:05 UTC). The full timeline and metric slices are in the attached incident stub and the RCA draft: https://drive.redwood.example/r/INC-20260414-rca-draft (internal link).

Credit outcome:
- Per Section 4.1 of the Master Service Agreement (MSA) and our standard credit calculation, the measured full-unavailability window results in a small prorated service credit.
- We'll apply a prorated credit equal to 0.01% of Greenleaf's APRIL invoice (rounded to the nearest dollar). This will appear on the next billing cycle. If you prefer an immediate manual credit, confirm and we can issue it sooner.

Next steps / timeline:
- RCA/postmortem (draft attached) — will share a finalized postmortem by EOD Friday (2026-04-17).
- Customer sync — if you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the RCA with our SRE and product leads next week.
- Preventive actions already in progress: stronger KV broker health checks, earlier fallback thresholds, and a targeted canary test on the affected pool.

Apologies again for the impact. We're committed to reducing recurrence and will follow up with a finalized postmortem and a short list of actionable mitigation steps.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
